judge_assessment.explanation: Every factual claim the judge makes is supported. I solved all twelve equations independently (5, 7, 8, -3, 16, 7, [19 then 6], 3, 15, 5, -6, 12) and re-ran the five substitution checks (9(7)+14=77, -3(3)+11=2, -4(-6)-9=15, 5(12-3)=45, and 6(4)-5=19 for Maya's rejected x=4); all match verify.json and the boxed key values. The judge is right that item 7's planted x=4 is rejected for the right reason and corrected to x=6, and right that no problem here has an open response — the "nothing flagged for manual review" claim in final_response.md is true on this sheet, unlike most of this batch. Where I part company is the artifact finding that the five-page worksheet is "spacious rather than defective" while the judge still deducted visual_and_print_quality to 3. The deduction is fair and has a traceable cause the judge did not name: scripts/page_budget.py computes ideal 4 pages for this content (81.2cm) but accepts anything up to 6 because SLACK_OVER is a flat +2, so the layout-ws gate passed a sheet a full page above its own budget with no signal to the author. Page 5 carries a single problem.

strengths_to_preserve: The substitution check is encoded, not just requested: problems 6, 8, 11 and 12 each carry a SECOND verify entry of type eval (9x+14 at x=7 → 77, -3x+11 at x=3 → 2, -4x-9 at x=-6 → 15, 5(x-3) at x=12 → 45), so the check the worksheet asks the student to perform is itself machine-verified rather than asserted.

Problem 7 turns checking into diagnosis: Maya's x=4 is evaluated (6(4)-5=19, not 31) as its own verify entry before the equation is solved correctly, and the declared trap (6-5)*x captures the specific misconception of combining 6 and 5 before multiplying.

The ramp reaches genuinely different shapes rather than rescaled copies: division form (x/4 + 6 = 10, and m/3 - 7 = -2 with a renamed variable), negative coefficients (-3x + 11 = 2, 12 - 5x = -13), and a bracketed form (5(x - 3) = 45) that is two-step only after distributing or dividing first.

root_causes.description: page_budget.py's cost model charges 2.0cm of front matter for "title + rule + instruction line", but every sheet this system produces opens with a wrapped subtitle and a four-to-five bullet directions block, and pages 2+ each carry a running "(continued)" header charged nowhere. The ideal therefore reads about one page low, and SLACK_OVER = 2 absorbs the error silently instead of surfacing it.
evidence: scripts/page_budget.py line 281: title_block_cm = 2.0 * scale; line 105: SLACK_OVER = 2.
python3 scripts/page_budget.py on this task's verify.json reports "ideal 4 page(s) · accepted range 2-6"; the compiled worksheet.pdf is 5 pages and gate layout-ws PASSED.

9 of the 10 sheets in this batch compile above their computed ideal (curr-174 4>3, curr-177 5>4, curr-178 4>3, curr-181 5>4, curr-190 5>4, curr-196 6>5, curr-197 7>5, curr-198 5>3, curr-199 4>3); only curr-170 lands on it.
The two cases in this batch that lost a visual_and_print_quality point (curr-177, curr-197) are the two overshoots with the least dense pages.

improvements.title: Charge the directions block and continuation headers in the page budget, and warn when the compiled sheet exceeds its own ideal
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes in scripts/page_budget.py. (1) Replace the flat 2.0cm front matter with a measured charge: when --from-tex is supplied, count the subtitle's wrapped lines and the directions/itemize block before the first \problem and charge their real height; add a per-continuation-page charge for the running header. (2) Keep SLACK_OVER as the failure threshold but have scripts/build.sh print an explicit "pages N > ideal M — trim a stem or drop a problem" warning whenever the compiled count exceeds ideal_pages, so the author sees the overshoot instead of a silent PASS.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_page_budget.py add a fixture ws.tex carrying a five-bullet directions block and assert budget(--from-tex) returns an ideal at least 1 greater than the same verify.json with a bare title; and assert build.sh emits the "> ideal" warning line for a 5-page compile against ideal 4. Both assertions fail today because the front matter is a constant and no warning exists.
improvements.expected_impact: The budget stops under-predicting by a page on essentially every sheet, so the accepted range brackets reality and authors are told to trim before delivery instead of after a reviewer deducts a point.
improvements.risk: Raising ideal_pages also raises max_pages, so a genuinely bloated sheet could slip further before failing; the warning has to be loud enough to compensate, and the existing page-budget fixtures need re-baselining.

case_summary: A correct, honest two-step-equation fluency set. All twelve solutions and all five substitution checks verify, the equation-plus-check pattern is encoded as two verify entries per problem rather than asserted in prose, and problem 7's planted x=4 is evaluated as its own check before being corrected to x=6. This is also the one sheet in my batch where "nothing is flagged for manual review" is literally true — every item has a single numeric answer. The single deducted point is layout: five pages for 81.2cm of content that budgets to four, with page 5 holding one problem. That is a gate blind spot rather than an authoring accident — page_budget.py charges 2cm of front matter for a page that actually carries a wrapped subtitle and a four-bullet directions box, and its flat +2 slack hides the overshoot. Stylistic note, not raised as a defect: problems 1, 3 and 6 are all ax + b = c with positive integers and whole-number roots, which sits close to the prompt's "without repeating an identical problem skeleton".
